ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow-white nuchal collar and a dark, V-shaped mark on the nape. It features a prominent subocular scale touching the eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Nilgiri Keelback is best distinguished by the prominent, bright yellow or orange nuchal collar located immediately behind its head, which contrasts sharply with its body.
ai.habitat: The Nilgiri Keelback inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests and shola-grassland mosaics of the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at elevations above 1,000m.
ai.behavior: The Nilgiri Keelback is primarily diurnal and semi-aquatic, frequently foraging for frogs and tadpoles in shallow streams and marshy areas within the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: Sahyadriophis beddomei is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sahyadriophis beddomei* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Maharashtra at elevations of 600–2,000 meters.
